subject: Estimate correlation / relation between random effects with a multivariate mode

messages.author: 3cfaef29dbc536f8
messages.subject: Estimate correlation / relation between random effects with a multivariate mode
parts:
Hi brms-users, a newcomer to brms / Stan, I'm trying to fit a multivariate model. In particular, I'm trying to figure out how youths' engagement, repeatedly measured (outcome #1), relates to changes in their future goals and plans, measured once, after the repeated measures (outcome #2), in the context of summer STEM programs. To give just a bit more context, the repeated measures outcome (outcome #1) is from an experience sampling method, whereas changes in future goals and plans (outcome #2) is measured using a self-report survey after youths' time in the programs (they also completed the same survey before the program). I'm curious about how students' experiences relate to changes in their outcomes (in this case their future goals and plans). 

If there are parts of this question that are technically or conceptually unclear, please do not hesitate to reach out to me to clarify - I apologize for any confusion and take responsibility for just not understanding this modeling approach quite well enough!

Initially, here's what I did. I used predictions from a mixed effects model (i.e., using the youth-level random effects predictions, or the youth-level BLUPs, using the lme4 package) in a second, separate model predicting changes (as I included a pre-program future goals and plans measure) in their future goals and plans. Following the advice of Houslay et al. (2017) (and Houslay's helpful tutorials), I am trying to estimate these two, separate models in a single model, initially and still using MCMCglmm and now also using brms, partially to learn about the use of brms and partiallyse as I'd like to compare across their (MCMCglmm and brms) results. 

I read the tutorial for estimating multivariate models with brms and am reaching out in this forum for help. To give a bit of a sense of what I've been doing with a mixed effects model, here is some of the code I have used with lme4:

     library(lme4)
     library(tidyverse)

m1 <- lmer(rm_engagement ~ 1 + (1 | participant_ID) + (1 | program_ID), data = d)

d_BLUP <- ranef(m1) %>% 
    pluck(1) %>% 
    rownames_to_column("participant_ID") %>% 
    mutate(participant_ID = as.integer(participant_ID)) %>% 
    rename(rm_engagement_BLUP = `(Intercept)`) 

d_ind_level <- distinct(d, participant_ID, post_interest, program_ID)
d_for_m2 <- left_join(d_ind_level, d_BLUP, by = "participant_ID")
d_for_m2 <- filter(d_for_m2, !is.na(post_interest))
    
m2 <- lmer(post_interest ~ 1 + rm_engagement_BLUP + (1 | program_ID), data = d_for_m2)


Here is as far as I got with brms, but it's not clear to me that I've specified the correlation between the two outcomes / specified this correctly.

library(brms)

d <- read_csv("ex-data.csv")

bf_rm_engagement <- bf(post_interest ~ 1 + (1 | participant_ID) + (1 | program_ID))
bf_interest <- bf(rm_engagement ~ 1 + (1 | program_ID))

fit <- brm(bf_rm_engagement + bf_interest, data = d, chains = 2, cores = 4)
fit

The data and code for this are available in this GitHub repository (in the lme4-example.Rmd) R markdown file. 

Thank you very much!
Josh

messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Estimate correlation / relation between random effects with a multivariate mode
parts:
I don't think brms can handle the model you have in mind within one step, because you have different number of rows per data.frame
and you effectively use the random effects of the first model in the predictions of the second. But I might be wrong.

Where you able to specify this correctly within one MCMCglmm model? If yes, it will likely be possible in brms as well.
